meta.description: Index of the papers and practitioner sources behind docs/literature-review.md and the pilots. Files in papers-original/, papers-md/ and web/ are private reading copies and gitignored, as are the code clones in code/ (listed in code/README.md, read only); this index is tracked. docs/papers/fetch_papers.py downloads open-access PDFs and writes docs/papers/README.md from it; docs/papers/check_papers.py validates it.

fields.id: Stable key: the file stem for downloaded papers, otherwise year-surname-titlewords
fields.year: Year of the version cited (first public version for preprints)
fields.title: Title of the version cited
fields.authors: Author surnames as in the paper, comma-separated
fields.taxonomy: Primary classification: l1 (approach family or contribution type) and l2 (strategy); values from meta.taxonomy
fields.contribution: All contribution types of the work; values from meta.vocabularies.contribution
fields.input: Input data the method works on; values from meta.vocabularies.input
fields.domain: Application domain of the work; one value from meta.vocabularies.domain
fields.country: Countries of the institutions in `institution`, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, deduplicated in order of first appearance (first author first); names in meta.vocabularies.country. Empty when no affiliation could be determined; independent researchers add no country
fields.institution: All author institutions, deduplicated in order of first appearance (first author first); canonical names from meta.vocabularies.institution, which maps each name to its country (null when it could not be determined), its OpenAlex/ROR type (education, company, government, facility, nonprofit, healthcare, archive, other) and its ROR URL (null when ROR has no record). Names are ROR display names, otherwise the name printed in the paper. Departments, labs and institutes without legal personality map to their parent (university department to the university, MPI for Informatics to the Max Planck Society, INSAIT to Sofia University, A*STAR institutes to A*STAR, joint CNRS units to the partners printed in the paper); company labs map to the company entity (per country where ROR has one); legally separate institutes stay (DFKI, Computer Vision Center, CAS institutes)
fields.affiliation_source: Where country and institution come from; values from meta.vocabularies.affiliation_source
fields.pdf: Open-access PDF URL, or null when not open access
fields.file: Local file in papers-original/ (or web/ for saved pages), or null
fields.code: Optional; official public code repositories of the work, each {url, licence, commit, local}: url is the repository; licence is the SPDX identifier of the LICENSE file, a short description for custom or mixed licences, or 'none' when the repository has no licence file (no reuse rights); commit is the full hash of the shallow clone that was read (null if not cloned); local is the clone under docs/papers/code/<owner>__<repo> (gitignored, read only, never run; null if not cloned). Unofficial ports and pipeline components are listed only in docs/papers/code/README.md
fields.note: One or two sentences: what the work does and what it means for this project
fields.kind: Only for non-papers: 'web' for saved web pages

Survey.description: Reviews of the field or of an adjacent one; no new method.

l2.Floor plan analysis: Surveys of floor plan or architectural drawing analysis.
l2.Adjacent field: Surveys of a neighbouring field (document analysis, map vectorisation, segmentation).

Classical and rule-based.description: Hand-designed image processing and rules, no learned model for the main task.

l2.Heuristic pipeline: Line and text separation, morphology, gap closing, rooms from connected regions.
l2.Statistical and structural recognition: Patch classifiers or statistical models feeding structural (graph) reasoning.

Raster parsing.description: Learned parsing of drawing images (pixels, keypoints, regions, text), then conversion to geometry, sheet structure or scale.

l2.Semantic segmentation: Pixel classes (walls, rooms, openings), single or multi-task; geometry derived afterwards.
l2.Segmentation and vectorisation: Segmentation or keypoints plus an explicit vectorisation step (integer programming, junction graphs, rules).
l2.Primitive vectorisation: Cleaning raster drawings and fitting lines, curves or closed shapes, without building semantics.
l2.Symbol and keypoint detection: Detectors or keypoint models for symbols, openings and layout regions.
l2.Sheet layout and title blocks: Detecting sheet regions (drawing views, title blocks, legends, notes, revision tables) and reading title blocks and view captions.
l2.Scale and dimension reading: Recovering metric scale from dimension strings, scale bars or scale notes; scale-bar methods from adjacent fields (microscopy, maps) are included and marked by their domain.

Structured prediction.description: Learned models that output graphs or polygons directly.

l2.Graph-based: Wall or room graphs predicted or classified with graph networks or autoregressive decoders.
l2.Polygon decoder: Room polygons as query sets, sequences or implicit fields (from drawings or scan density maps).

Vector CAD parsing.description: Models on vector primitives (lines, arcs, text, layers) of CAD drawings or vector PDFs, mostly learned.

l2.Panoptic symbol spotting: Class and instance per primitive; scored with panoptic quality on FloorPlanCAD-style data.
l2.Primitive graph segmentation: Primitives as graph nodes classified into walls, rooms or regions.
l2.Layer and entity classification: Classifying CAD layers, blocks or entities by their content rather than their names, to select the geometry to parse.

Vision-language models and agents.description: Multimodal language models fine-tuned or orchestrated for drawings.

l2.Fine-tuned VLM: A VLM trained to emit structured plan output (vectors, JSON).
l2.Agentic pipeline: LLM or VLM agents orchestrating tools, rules and humans.

Text recognition.description: Text detection and recognition, and its use on drawings.

l2.OCR system: General OCR engines and their technical reports.
l2.Decoding and lexicons: Constrained decoding and dictionary methods for recognisers.
l2.Text in technical drawings: OCR and text parsing specialised for engineering or architectural drawings.

Learning strategies.description: Training and adaptation methods from adjacent fields that transfer to plan parsing.

l2.Domain adaptation: Unsupervised domain adaptation and self-training from a labelled to an unlabelled domain.
l2.Synthetic data and domain generalisation: Procedural or synthetic training data and randomisation for unseen styles.
l2.Topology-aware learning: Losses, architectures or benchmarks for topologically correct thin structures.
l2.Annotation strategy: How to label efficiently: protocols, class design, label budgets.

Datasets and benchmarks.description: Data or evaluation protocols as the primary contribution.

l2.Vector plan dataset: Vector plans or CAD drawings with labels or graphs.
l2.Other drawing dataset: Engineering, structural or other technical drawings.
l2.Benchmark: Evaluation protocols and test sets for methods or models (VLM QA, vectorisation, topology).

Practitioner sources.description: Grey literature: vendor descriptions of working pipelines; not peer-reviewed.

l2.Vendor pipeline: Vendor tutorials, solution pages and model guides.

contribution.method: A new model, algorithm or pipeline
contribution.dataset: A new dataset or data release
contribution.benchmark: An evaluation protocol, test set or comparative evaluation
contribution.system: A software system, engine or technical report of a toolkit

input.structured layout: Graphs, JSON or other symbolic layout descriptions

papers.title: MMArch: Benchmarking multimodal reasoning grounded in architectural evidence
papers.note: 1,212 short-answer items built from figures in architecture and civil-engineering papers (ten subdomains from structures and seismic to heritage, urban and BIM); best proprietary MLLM 52%, best open model about 30%, experts 95%. Tests principle-grounded reasoning over AEC figures, not plan parsing; context for how far VLMs are from expert reading

papers.title: When should a network emit geometry, and when should it detect it? Readout, reconciliation, and representation in floorplan vectorization

code.licence: none (README only; it declares MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for ResPlan-FP, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the skv4 labels)

papers.note: Same trained network read out as an autoregressive coordinate sequence or as junction/centreline heatmaps assembled into a graph: detection wins on real CubiCasa5K scans (+2.7 to +5.1 wall F1), fusing both outputs adds about 7 points; releases an edit-cost metric, corrected CubiCasa5K labels (skv4) and ResPlan-FP (16,998 plans rendered from ResPlan). Licences per the fpvec-lab README: code MIT, ResPlan-FP data CC BY 4.0, skv4 labels CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (inherited from CubiCasa5K, research use only); on 7 Oct 2026 the repository held only the README. Supports a detection readout plus fusion; ResPlan-FP is a redistributable test set

papers.title: FloorPlan-VLN: A new paradigm for floor plan guided vision-language navigation
institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
papers.note: Navigation with semantic floor plans as global priors: over 10k episodes in 72 Matterport3D scenes with more than 100 annotated plans; FP-Nav fine-tunes Qwen-2.5-VL on egocentric frames concatenated with the rasterised plan (over 60% relative gain in success rate). A downstream consumer of parsed plans, not a parsing method

papers.title: Text detection on technical drawings for the digitization of brown-field processes
papers.note: Faster R-CNN text detector and Keras-OCR recogniser, both trained on a domain-knowledge generator of artificial technical drawings plus few real ones; beats out-of-the-box Keras-OCR on vertical text and drawing symbols. Supports synthetic training data for our dimension-text detector

papers.title: Automated parsing of engineering drawings for structured information extraction using a fine-tuned document understanding transformer
institution: Agency for Science, Technology and Research
papers.note: YOLOv11-OBB finds nine annotation types (GD&T, tolerances, measures, notes, title blocks and others) on 1,367 public mechanical drawings, a fine-tuned Donut parses each crop to JSON; one shared model beats per-class models, but the headline F1 of 97.3% is for the GD&T class only (title blocks 72.9%, notes 83.1%). OCR-free crop-then-parse pattern for annotation blocks; the annotated drawings are not released

papers.title: An efficient deep learning framework for text detection and recognition in engineering drawings
papers.note: Slimmed DBNet detector (3.8M parameters) plus a transformer recogniser for rebar annotations on construction drawings: detection precision 94.2% (recall 97.2%, F1 95.9%); the 96.3% recognition accuracy is measured on ground-truth text crops, not after detection. Drawings from PowerChina HDEC projects; the release statements conflict (annotated crops, weights and code promised, the data availability statement says available on request). Recipe for a small detector-recogniser pair for dimension strings

papers.title: Automatic floor plan analysis and recognition
papers.note: Review of rule-based and learning-based floor plan analysis on raster images from 1995 to 2021 (walls, doors, rooms, vectorisation, modelling) with datasets, scopes and tasks; the most cited survey of the field. Not open access

papers.title: Symbol spotting for architectural drawings: state-of-the-art and new industry-driven developments
papers.venue: IPSJ Transactions on Computer Vision and Applications 11, 2, doi:10.1186/s41074-019-0055-1
papers.note: Review of symbol spotting in architectural drawing images: methods reach good recall but poor precision on dense real drawings; proposes template matching with a clutter-tolerant cross-correlation. Background for door, window and fixture detection on our plans

papers.title: A comprehensive survey of floor plan image analysis and related applications
institution: Sardar Vallabhbhai National Institute of Technology Surat
papers.note: Survey of floor plan image analysis that sorts models into nine families (dimensional, room-based, structural, retrieval, object detection, graph, map, residential, area-based) and compares them by dataset, year and reported metrics; most recent journal survey of the field. Not open access

papers.title: Deep learning-based text detection and recognition on architectural floor plans
papers.note: Two-stage text extraction on floor plan images: an object detector finds text boxes and an OCR recogniser reads them; a model comparison picks YOLOv7 for detection and PARSeq for recognition, a new floor plan dataset with text bounding boxes is built, and domain-specific synthetic training data clearly improves detection. For our room stamps (multi-field, German text) it supports detecting each stamp line as its own box and fine-tuning the recogniser on synthetic German stamp text instead of reading whole stamps with general OCR; whether it handles stacked multi-field stamps is not known from the abstract. Not open access (summary from the publisher abstract and citing papers, full text not read)

papers.title: Benchmarking deep learning approaches for AEC engineering drawing layout detection and information extraction
papers.note: FELD: 551 façade drawing sheets at 300 dpi with nine layout classes (title block, revision table, legend, notes, elevation, sections, GA plan); RF-DETR is best (mAP50 0.949, title block mAP50:95 0.989), Qwen3-VL-8B with LoRA reaches the best F1 (0.911) but takes seconds per sheet, and document-layout pretraining (DocLayout-YOLO) hurts ("domain interference"). Closest analogue of our sheet-layout stage: train a COCO-initialised detector on our own sheets; inputs downscaled to 1,344 × 800 px, no data or code released

papers.title: Title block detection and information extraction for enhanced building drawings search
papers.authors: Lombardi, Duan, Elnagar, Zaalouk, Ismail, Vakaj
papers.note: Faster R-CNN (MobileNetV3) detects title block, main content, legend and notes on 1,385 building engineering drawings (title-block accuracy 0.971), then GPT-4o reads the cropped title block; rule baselines, table-structure models and GPT-4o on the whole sheet fail on hard historical drawings. Detect, crop, then read; the cloud reader must be replaced by a self-hosted one for internal plans; no code or data released

papers.title: Open-source VLMs for engineering drawing metadata: QWEN-VL title-block detection and information extraction
papers.note: Qwen2.5-VL-3B with LoRA grounds title blocks ("Plankopf") on German bridge drawings (F1 93.8% on 64 test drawings vs 93.1% for YOLOv11-m, which gives tighter boxes; zero-shot grounding failed) and reads scale, drawing name and route from the crop: the Maßstab field reaches word accuracy 0.990 after fine-tuning vs 0.572 zero-shot. Evidence that a small self-hosted VLM can read German-language title-block scales; base model licence "qwen-research", data confidential, no code

papers.title: AI-based extraction and management of text and view information from 2D bridge engineering drawings
papers.note: YOLOv7 detects the views on 2,000 German bridge drawings (validation mAP@.5 about 0.92), Handprint OCR reads printed and handwritten text, and view titles found by k-means on font height are matched to views by containment, intersection or nearest centre, so each view is cropped and named ("Draufsicht", "Schnitt A-A"). Recipe for several drawings per sheet, each with its own caption and scale; CC BY

papers.title: ICDAR 2021 competition on historical map segmentation
institution: École Pour l'Informatique et les Techniques Avancées
Institut national de l’information géographique et forestière
École des hautes études en sciences sociales
Institut National des Sciences Appliquées de Lyon
University of West Bohemia in Pilsen
papers.note: Three tasks on Paris atlas sheets (1894–1937): building-block detection given an input mask of the map area, segmentation of the map content area from the sheet scored by the 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (won by a U-Net-like FCN plus binarisation), and detection of georeferencing-line intersections. Method source for drawing-region masks and their boundary metric; data CC BY 4.0

papers.title: EXSCLAIM!: Harnessing materials science literature for self-labeled microscopy datasets
papers.note: Toolkit that mines journal figures, separates subfigures and labels them from captions; its scale module detects scale bars and their labels with Faster R-CNN, reads the label with a CRNN and pairs bars and labels by box-centre distance (bar length MAE 5.4%, 82% of labels read on 440 figures, per the evidence brief). Method source for our scale-bar reader from an adjacent field (microscopy); code GPL-3.0, so reimplement. Download blocked, open access at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2023.100843 (PMC10682750)

papers.title: Towards a robust deep learning-based scale inference approach in construction drawings
papers.venue: Computing in Civil Engineering 2023 (ASCE i3CE), pp. 721–728, doi:10.1061/9780784485248.087
papers.note: YOLOv7 localises dimension lines, EasyOCR reads their values and the pixel resolution is found by voting over the pairs; only "promising results" are stated, no figures obtained. The only paper found that infers drawing scale itself; same group as the floor plan OCR of Schönfelder et al. Not open access

papers.title: Raster image-based house-type recognition and three-dimensional reconstruction technology
papers.note: Keypoint detection (CPN-Floor) of walls, doors and windows with rule-based candidate filtering on more than 5,000 annotated house plans (over 87% precision, 88% recall), a WebGL 3D viewer, and scale from the dimension strips: YOLOv8 plus Shi–Tomasi corners find the measurement endpoints, OFA-OCR reads the values and outlying per-dimension scales are dropped ("scale calculation accuracy exceeding 95%", metric not defined). Template for dimension-strip scale with outlier rejection; no code. Download blocked, open access at https://www.mdpi.com/2075-5309/15/7/1178

papers.title: A hybrid deep learning and rule-based method for architectural drawing vectorization and CAD reconstruction
papers.note: Scanned historical architectural drawings to editable CAD: YOLOv11n detects dimension annotations, dimension endpoints and axis-grid markers (mAP50 0.98–0.99), PaddleOCR reads 89.3% of dimension and 91.0% of axis texts, one mm/px estimate per dimension is combined by RANSAC, then rules rebuild the line topology snapped to a 50 mm module (figures per the evidence brief; one worked example). Recipe for dimension-based scale and grid axes on scans; detector is AGPL Ultralytics, no code. Download blocked, open access at https://www.mdpi.com/2075-5309/16/5/1043

papers.title: Automated dimension-aware 2D-to-BIM reconstruction through cross-modal text-geometry alignment
papers.note: Legacy floor plans to IFC: OCR of dimension texts (90.2% exact), OCR-guided denoising and segmentation, then a metric grid rebuilt from the annotations: the pixel-to-metric ratio is the median of OCR value over pixel gap, each grid spacing is checked and corrected, totals are matched against cumulative spacings, and the plan is scaled separately along x and y; 62 of 200 plans fully correct, with an IFC-based evaluation. Model for robust dimension-string scale with anisotropy; extended journal version doi:10.1016/j.autcon.2026.107204; no code

papers.title: BlueprintAgent: Constraint-triggered targeted revisits for simulation-ready generation from scanned structural blueprints
papers.note: Multimodal-LLM agent that extracts reinforced-concrete frame models from 300 real scanned structural sheets of 20 projects: a CV probe finds grid label circles and lines, the MLLM reads the labels, and engineering validators (span ratios, cross-floor axis consistency) trigger targeted re-reads of local regions; axis F1 1.000 vs 0.987 for a single zero-shot MLLM. Pattern for validator-triggered re-reading and cross-storey grid consistency; the paper states no data release

papers.title: Automatic layer classification method-based elevation recognition in architectural drawings for reconstruction of 3D BIM models
papers.authors: Yin, Tang, Zhou, Wen, Xu, Deng
papers.note: Classifies the layers of CAD drawings by their content rather than their names (ALCM), then recognises elevation views, floor levels and opening offsets and heights to build a façade BIM model: nearly all floor levels found and 88% of visible members measured perfectly on 94 drawings. Layer names are at best a weak feature for our DWG input; classify layers by content. Not open access
